curator_notes: [Tier 4 -- mechanical heuristic, NOT a verified resistance-mechanism claim] DIMETHYL-FUMARATE's DepMap-supplied target/mechanism annotation ('KEAP1 LIKE (NRF2) ACTIVATOR, NUCLEAR FACTOR ERYTHROID DERIVED') contains the keyword 'NRF2', which this build's keyword list maps to the nrf2_ferroptosis signature panel. Glucose restriction (5% of standard medium glucose) induces a nrf2_ferroptosis signature (death_promoting) in T47D_BREAST. This is a purely textual co-occurrence between the drug's own mechanism of action and the modifier's induced pathway category -- it is NOT a claim that either affects the other's resistance, has not been reviewed by a curator, and predicts no direction (recorded as interaction_type = unknown). Treat as a keyword-matched lead for someone to investigate, not as evidence.

mechanism.notes: Glucose-deprivation DEGs implicated the NRF2-ferroptosis axis in T47D (GSE153830 series summary). [Real DEG backfill 2026-09-22: ssGSEA-style z-score 4.117 for gene set 'HALLMARK_REACTIVE_OXYGEN_SPECIES_PATHWAY' (49 genes measured), computed from 2 treatment vs 2 control real GSE153830 samples. This is a simple, uncorrected standardized-mean-difference statistic, not the paper's own (likely multiple-testing-corrected) pathway enrichment test -- a large |z| here does not necessarily mean the paper would call it significant, and vice versa. Treat as a real, reproducible number, not a replication of the paper's own significance call. See synlethality/signature_correlation.py for the method and its documented deviation from ssGSEA/GSVA proper.]

evidence_tier_definition.definition: The lowest-confidence tier in this database. A mechanical keyword match between a compound's own DepMap-supplied target/mechanism-of-action text and a modifier's induced-signature panel category -- not a cited, per-drug resistance-mechanism claim (see Tier 3), not reviewed by a curator, and not a prediction of direction (interaction_type is always 'unknown' here). Treat as 'worth someone checking,' not evidence.

related.curator_notes: Modifier leg: glucose deprivation engaged the NRF2-ferroptosis axis in T47D (GSE153830; Zhang et al. 2021). Drug leg: metformin induces ferroptosis in breast cancer cells via SLC7A11 UFMylation inhibition (Yang et al. 2021). No combination viability readout exists in either study — inferred via shared ferroptosis mechanism.

related.curator_notes: [Mechanistic Bridging -- model-generated hypothesis, not a tested result] Glucose restriction (5% of standard medium glucose) induces a nrf2_ferroptosis signature (death_promoting) in T47D; Erastin's reported resistance mechanism runs through the same pathway (GPX4-dependent lipid-peroxide detoxification). Because the modifier's effect on this pathway is death-promoting (suppresses the pathway the drug's resistance depends on), this is surfaced as a synergy candidate. This combination has not been evaluated together in any cited study -- it is a candidate for testing, generated by matching independently-curated signature and resistance-mechanism evidence, not a direct or inferred empirical finding.

resistance_mechanism.mechanism_description: GPX4 detoxifies lipid peroxides downstream of cystine/glutathione depletion; sufficient GPX4 activity (or an intact glutathione pool feeding it) can rescue cells from erastin's system Xc- blockade despite cystine starvation (Dixon et al. 2012; Yang et al. 2014).
